title: Tanzanian Tomato and Onion Salad
author: Mama Salima
desc: Tanzanian Kachumbari — fresh tomatoes, red onion, and green chilli tossed with lemon juice, coriander, and salt. Tanzania's equivalent of the East African kachumbari — the fresh salad that accompanies nyama choma, pilau, and ugali.
longDesc: Kachumbari is as Tanzanian as it is Kenyan — the shared Swahili coastal salad tradition produces identical preparations in both countries. The tomatoes must be ripe and firm, the onion wafer-thin, and the lemon generous.
ingredients: 1 medium red onion — very thinly sliced
3 tbsp fresh lemon or lime juice
steps: Slice onion as thinly as possible.
Combine tomatoes, onion, and chilli in a bowl.
Add lemon juice, coriander, salt, and pepper.
Serve immediately — do not rest long or tomatoes become watery.
chefTips: Wafer-thin onion is the signature — use a sharp knife or mandoline.
Ripe but firm tomatoes only — soft tomatoes become watery immediately.
cookingScience: Salt draws water from the tomato and onion cells through osmosis — after 15 minutes the kachumbari becomes watery as the cells release their fluid. Serving immediately preserves the fresh, bright texture.
sustainabilityTips: Locally grown Tanzanian tomatoes, onions, and lemons.
healthBenefits: Very high vitamin C from tomatoes and lemon.
culturalNote: Kachumbari is the condiment that makes every Tanzanian meal more alive — the fresh acidity and brightness that cuts through the richness of pilau, the fat of nyama choma, and the starch of ugali.
